public_contract: Submission retains the complete public-source target and dependency snapshot, provenance, and required license texts without compiled artifacts.
The target, public spawn dependency, and an external consumer of all three published config natives compile with the pinned SourceMod toolchain.
The submitted L4D Infected Bots plugin loads and publishes its library in a real server boot.
For the observed server capacity and live-survivor population, sm_zlimit accepts the exact remaining client slots without a legacy extra-slot reservation.
A request already below the remaining capacity is preserved through the public sm_zlimit command path.
The submitted library loads with exactly one live survivor so count-profile selection is unambiguous.
Without a current-map profile, Settings count values overlay Settings default values across integer, float, and string config natives.
Keys omitted by the Settings count profile retain their Settings default values.
Public sm_zlimit and sm_timer commands temporarily override the active values before a reload.
Reload clears command overrides and activates the current Maps default/count profile, including inheritance for omitted count keys.
The target and public spawn-provider dependency load in controlled-zombie mode.
A live survivor and infected victim are created after round initialization in the real versus server fixture.
Observe the first living replacement continuously; an initial-window death must not advance the wave before round_start plus eight seconds (public scheduling lower bound, two ticks tolerance).
The deferred initial-window replacement eventually produces a live infected bot.
After the initial window resets, a later victim death again replenishes on the normal one-second delay.
The target and public spawn-provider dependency load for the finale lifecycle fixture.
The finale_win event and public allow-cvar disable/re-enable lifecycle remain usable before the observed death sequence.
finale_win cancels a pending infected replacement so no bot appears after the configured delay.
